title: Your body glows in the dark. Cameras caught it 🌙
subject: glow
description:
Which part of your body do you think glows brightest? 👇

Humans emit ultraweak visible light, 1,000 times too faint for our eyes. In 2009, Japanese researchers photographed it in total darkness. In 2025, a University of Calgary team showed the glow from living mice drops sharply after death.

Sources: Kobayashi, Kikuchi & Okamura, "Imaging of Ultraweak Spontaneous Photon Emission from Human Body Displaying Diurnal Rhythm", PLoS ONE (2009); Live Science, "Strange! Humans Glow in Visible Light" (2009); National Geographic, "Photographing the glow of the human body" (Ed Yong, 2009); Salari et al., The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters (2025); University of Calgary, "UCalgary scientists go viral with study that shows all living things emit an eerie glow" (2025); ScienceAlert (2026).
tags: does the human body emit light

scenes.text: Your face is glowing right now.
In 2009, Masaki Kobayashi's team in Japan filmed 5 men in total darkness with cameras that count single photons.
The light is 1,000 times too weak for your eyes. Cheeks and lips shine brightest, peaking around 4 p.m.
It likely comes from free radicals made by your metabolism.
In 2025, Vahid Salari's team in Calgary filmed mice for an hour alive, then an hour after death.
Alive, they glowed. After death, the light dropped sharply.
